summary: 41-year-old man with HIV (CD4 140, detectable viral load, poor ART adherence) and a perianal abscess. Drain; antibiotics are indicated in immunosuppression; send pus for culture and tissue for histology (atypical infection, anal neoplasia); re-engage HIV care.

inputs.hpi: Four days of perianal pain and swelling. HIV diagnosed 8 years ago; stopped antiretrovirals 6 months ago; last CD4 140. Previous perianal warts treated. No fevers, bowels normal.

exam.general: Thin. Temperature 37.4°C, HR 88, BP 118/74. Oral candida.
exam.other: Perianal: 3 cm tender fluctuant swelling at 9 o’clock with 1 cm of erythema; scarring from previous warts; no ulcer, no mass on DRE.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Perianal abscess in advanced HIV
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Perianal abscess at 9 o’clock in a patient with HIV, CD4 140, off ART. Drainage, antibiotics, pus culture and wall biopsy; HIV clinic referral.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Anal cancer is not a PANE disease; symptom inference ranks anal SCC #2.

emergencyLevel.note: Same rule as the base case: an undrained abscess is drained promptly; immunosuppression makes delay more dangerous.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web adaptiveTriage has no perianal abscess/anorectal sepsis rule: the level depends on the pain score and incidental words (the base abscess reaches "emergency" only via the negated "no weight loss" plus pain 8/10; with pain 6/10 it is routine).
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Add an anorectal-sepsis triage rule (perianal/perineal pain + swelling/lump, or "abscess") → at least same_day_call, and emergency_now with fever + SIRS, diabetes, immunosuppression or spreading erythema.

redFlags.note: The immunosuppression has to be surfaced: it changes antibiotic use and the differential.
redFlags.knownGapNote: HIV/immunosuppression in the comorbidity list is not surfaced by triage, prompts or the perianal_abscess protocol (whose IV antibiotic line mentions "immunocompromised" only as an indication).
redFlags.proposedFix: Surface HIV/low CD4/biologics/chemotherapy as an immunosuppression flag (triage comorbidity regex + a clinical prompt).

guideline.section: Antibiotics after drainage in immunosuppressed patients; cultures in atypical/immunosuppressed cases
guideline.citation: Gaertner WB, Burgess PL, Davids JS, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, and rectovaginal fistula. Dis Colon Rectum. 2022;65:964–985.

guideline.citation: Stewart DB, Gaertner WB, Glasgow SC, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for anal squamous cell cancers (revised 2018). Dis Colon Rectum. 2018;61:755–774.

rationale: Permutation: immunosuppression (HIV). The HIV status is in the comorbidity list; tests whether it is surfaced and whether antibiotics (then indicated) appear.
